newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-firm - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-firm - dealers.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Wednesday were seen steady, possibly firm, amid expectations for higher pork prices, livestock dealers said.
Pork prices were seen bolstered by strong demand and light production early this week, they said.
Top prices for hogs delivered to the plant in Iowa and southern Minnesota were expected at $54.50 to $55.00 per cwt.
Illinois top prices at plants could range $53.50 to $54.00 and top prices in Indiana/Ohio were seen at $53.00 to $53.50, sources in those areas said.
Pork prices at midday were mixed, but strong movement spurred ideas prices would strengthen later in the day, market sources said.

Fresh loin prices near midday were firm and hams weighing 17-20 lbs sold up $1.00 to $2.00 per cwt, while pork bellies were mixed, according to USDA. There were 43.0 pork loads and 15.0 loads of trimmings sold.

Hog slaughter Tuesday was pegged at 360,000 head, which brought the week to date figure to 681,000, USDA said. The week to date number was 4.3 percent below a week ago and 3.8 percent below a year ago.
